name: Open Targets Platform
description: Target-disease association evidence aggregated from genetics, omics, literature and known drugs; the standard first stop for target triage.

name: DepMap
description: Genome-wide CRISPR and RNAi essentiality across ~1,100 cancer cell lines, plus expression, mutation and drug-sensitivity data.

name: Pharos / TCRD
description: NIH IDG portal ranking the druggable genome by how well each target is studied (Tclin/Tchem/Tbio/Tdark).

name: UniProt
description: Reference protein sequence and functional annotation; the identifier backbone every other resource maps to.

name: Ensembl
description: Genome annotation, variation, comparative genomics and the BioMart/REST query layer over them.

name: Human Protein Atlas
description: Tissue, single-cell, subcellular and pathology protein expression maps; used to check target expression and off-tissue risk.

name: GTEx Portal
description: Bulk and single-nucleus expression and eQTL data across 50+ human tissues.

name: cBioPortal
description: Interactive exploration of large-scale cancer genomics studies (mutation, CNA, expression, survival).

name: STRING
description: Protein-protein association networks combining experiments, co-expression, text mining and orthology transfer.

name: BioGRID
description: Curated protein, genetic and chemical interactions from primary literature.

name: OmniPath
description: Unified signalling network: pathways, enzyme-substrate, complexes and annotations from 100+ resources, with a Python client.

name: Reactome
description: Peer-reviewed pathway database with pathway enrichment and network analysis tools.

name: KEGG
description: Pathway, disease and drug maps; free for academic web use, licensed for bulk download.

name: GSEA / MSigDB
description: Gene set enrichment analysis and the curated hallmark/canonical gene set collections behind it.

name: Enrichr
description: Fast web enrichment against 200+ gene set libraries, with an API.

name: g:Profiler
description: Functional enrichment, ortholog mapping and ID conversion with a stable versioned API.

name: DisGeNET
description: Gene-disease and variant-disease association collection used for target-indication rationale.

name: GeneCards
description: Aggregated gene-centric annotation across ~150 sources; free for academic browsing.

name: RCSB PDB
description: The experimental structure archive plus search, validation and ligand chemistry services.

name: AlphaFold Protein Structure DB
description: Predicted structures for 200M+ proteins with per-residue pLDDT confidence.

name: AlphaFold 3
description: Joint structure prediction for proteins, nucleic acids, ligands and ions; weights are available for non-commercial use on request.

name: Chai-1
description: Open multimodal biomolecular complex prediction model, free for commercial use.

name: MODELLER
description: Comparative/homology modelling by satisfaction of spatial restraints; free academic licence.

name: SWISS-MODEL
description: Automated homology modelling server with quality estimation (QMEANDisCo) and oligomeric state prediction.

name: MMseqs2
description: Ultra-fast sequence search and clustering; the MSA engine behind ColabFold.

name: HH-suite3
description: HMM-HMM remote homology detection for hard templates and deep MSAs.

name: PDBFixer
description: Repairs PDB files for simulation: missing residues and heavy atoms, non-standard residues, protonation, solvation.

name: PDB2PQR / APBS
description: Assigns titration states and charges/radii, then solves Poisson-Boltzmann electrostatics.

name: PROPKA
description: Empirical pKa prediction for protein residues and ligands, used to set protonation before docking or MD.

name: Biopython
description: General bioinformatics library: sequence and structure parsing, alignment, PDB handling.

name: DSSP
description: Reference secondary-structure and solvent-accessibility assignment from 3D coordinates.

name: CheckMyMetal
description: Validates metal sites in deposited or refined structures against expected coordination number, geometry and donor distances. Mis-assigned metals are common; check before you build a docking model on one.

name: AlphaFill
description: Transplants ligands, cofactors and metal ions into AlphaFold models by sequence and structure similarity. AlphaFold predicts the fold, not the metal, so a metalloprotein model without this step has an empty site.

name: ColabFold
description: AlphaFold2 and friends with MMseqs2 doing the MSA, which turns an overnight job into minutes; the usual way people actually run structure prediction.

name: fpocket
description: Voronoi-based pocket detection and druggability scoring, with mdpocket for pocket dynamics over MD trajectories.

name: P2Rank
description: Machine-learning ligand-binding site prediction from structure; fast, template-free, used inside several docking pipelines.

name: PrankWeb
description: Web front end for P2Rank with conservation scoring and in-browser visualisation.

name: CASTp
description: Computed atlas of surface topography: analytic pocket and cavity measurement.

name: ProteinsPlus / DoGSiteScorer
description: Pocket detection with druggability scores, plus protonation (Protoss) and pose analysis tools.

name: MetalPDB
description: Every metal site in the PDB, abstracted into minimal functional sites so you can compare coordination geometry and donor sets across unrelated folds.

name: MESPEUS
description: Metal coordination geometry measured across the PDB: bond lengths, angles and donor-set frequencies per metal. The reference for judging whether a site's geometry is physically reasonable.

name: MIB2
description: Predicts metal ion-binding residues and models the ion into the structure, by fragment transfer from known sites; covers a dozen biologically common ions.

name: Metal3D
description: 3D CNN predicting zinc site location and probability density directly from protein geometry; useful when the apo structure has no ion modelled.

name: BioMetAll
description: Geometry-based search for candidate metal-binding sites using only backbone and side-chain positions, so it finds sites in apo and predicted structures. This is the published v1; v2 adds scoring and metal discrimination.

name: BioMetAll v2
description: The current BioMetAll: adds a score per candidate site, discriminates between metals rather than reporting any site, and uses side-chain descriptors instead of backbone geometry alone.

name: BioBrigit
description: Predicts how a metal ion travels through a protein to reach its site, not just where the site is. Combines a 3D CNN over the biochemical environment with known bioinorganic coordination preferences.

name: LMetalSite
description: Alignment-free metal-binding residue prediction from sequence alone, via a protein language model; the fallback when there is no structure at all.

name: ZincBind
description: Curated database of zinc binding sites extracted from the PDB, grouped by coordinating residue family and site type.

name: InterMetalDB
description: Intermolecular metal sites, where the ion bridges two chains or a chain and a ligand; the place to look before assuming a metal-mediated contact is an artefact.

name: RDKit
description: The open cheminformatics toolkit everything else is built on: descriptors, fingerprints, conformers, substructure search, reaction handling.

name: AutoDock Vina
description: The most widely used open docking engine; fast, well-validated, and the baseline every other method is measured against.

name: OpenMM
description: GPU-accelerated MD as a Python library rather than a monolithic binary — the easiest engine to script custom simulation protocols around.

name: Foldseek
description: Structure search at sequence-search speed; finds structural homologues across the whole PDB and AlphaFold DB in seconds.

name: ProteinMPNN
description: Inverse folding: given a backbone, designs sequences that fold to it. The workhorse of modern de novo protein design.

name: RFdiffusion
description: Diffusion-based generation of protein backbones, including binders to a specified target site.

name: AiZynthFinder
description: Monte-Carlo tree search retrosynthesis over learned templates, with building-block availability built into the search.

name: ADMET-AI
description: Fast Chemprop-RDKit ADMET predictions across the TDC endpoint set, with percentile context against approved drugs.

name: PoseBusters
description: Checks whether a predicted pose is physically possible at all — geometry, stereochemistry, clashes with the protein. The standard sanity gate for generated poses.

name: ProLIF
description: Protein-ligand interaction fingerprints from structures or trajectories, so poses can be compared on interactions rather than score.

name: ABodyBuilder3
description: Fast, accurate antibody Fv structure prediction with per-residue confidence on the CDR loops.

name: REINVENT4
description: AstraZeneca's production generative design framework: reinforcement learning over a multi-parameter scoring function, with scaffold and linker modes.

name: DiffSBDD
description: Equivariant diffusion generating ligands directly inside a protein pocket.

name: TargetDiff
description: 3D diffusion model for structure-based ligand generation; a common baseline for pocket-conditioned design.

name: NeuralPLexer
description: Predicts protein-ligand complex structures directly, generating the receptor conformation alongside the pose instead of docking into a fixed one.

name: KarmaDock
description: Deep-learning docking that scores and optimises poses in one pass, fast enough to make a neural method viable for library-scale screening.

name: SurfDock
description: Surface-informed diffusion docking: conditions pose generation on the molecular surface of the pocket rather than atoms alone.

name: AIMNet2
description: Neural network potential covering neutral, charged and open-shell organic molecules across most of the periodic table — QM-quality energies at force-field cost.

name: Auto3D
description: Turns SMILES into low-energy 3D structures with correct stereochemistry and tautomer handling — the unglamorous step that silently ruins docking when skipped.

name: mmpdb
description: Matched molecular pair database from RDKit: extracts which single transformations have been made across a dataset and what they did to a property. The most directly medicinal-chemistry tool in the open stack.

name: Lilly Medchem Rules
description: Eli Lilly's published rule set for rejecting compounds a medicinal chemist would not take forward — reactive groups, known frequent hitters, unstable motifs. A harder filter than PAINS alone.

name: Fragmenstein
description: Merges and places fragment hits into a single compound that respects the crystallographic positions they came from — built for fragment-based campaigns and XChem-style data.

name: ScaffoldGraph
description: Builds scaffold trees and networks over a library, so you can see which chemotypes a screening set actually covers and where a series sits.

name: MolFormer
description: IBM's transformer pretrained on a billion molecules; a strong general-purpose embedding when you have too little labelled data to train from scratch.

name: ChemBERTa
description: BERT-style pretraining over SMILES — the accessible baseline for whether a pretrained representation beats fingerprints on your endpoint.

name: Chemformer
description: Sequence-to-sequence transformer for reaction prediction and retrosynthesis, pretrained on SMILES and fine-tuned per task.

name: OpenADMET
description: Open consortium generating new experimental ADMET data on the targets that break programmes, and releasing models trained on it — an answer to ADMET models trained on stale public sets.

name: PROTAC-DB
description: Curated database of PROTACs with ternary complex data, linker chemistry and measured degradation — the reference set for degrader design.

name: SwissTargetPrediction
description: Predicts a small molecule's likely protein targets by combining 2D and 3D similarity to compounds with measured activity. The web standard for a first pass, with the caveat that it can only propose targets that already have ligands.

name: PPB2
description: Polypharmacology Browser 2: nearest-neighbour search over ChEMBL by ECfp4, Xfp shape-pharmacophore or MQN fingerprints, optionally combined with a naive Bayes model fitted on the fly. Useful because you can compare what different descriptors nominate.

name: TargetNet
description: Runs a per-target QSAR model across 623 human proteins and returns a predicted activity profile rather than a ranked shortlist. Each target carries its own model, so applicability varies target by target.

name: ChEMBL multitask target prediction
description: ChEMBL's own multitask neural network for target prediction, shipped as a model you run locally instead of a web form. Trained on ChEMBL activities, with runnable examples in Python, C++, Julia and JavaScript.

name: SEA
description: Similarity Ensemble Approach: relates targets by the chemistry of their ligands, so a compound's likely off-targets fall out of its structure. Long-standing polypharmacology check.

name: SwissBioisostere
description: Which substituent replacements have actually been made and what they did to activity, mined from measured data — bioisosteric replacement grounded in evidence rather than intuition.

name: RXNMapper
description: Atom-maps reactions from an attention-based model with no templates — the preprocessing step that template extraction and most reaction ML quietly depend on.

name: Molecular Transformer
description: Sequence-to-sequence forward reaction prediction: given reactants, predict the product. The model most later reaction work is benchmarked against.

name: Retro*
description: Neural A* search over retrosynthesis trees, optimising the whole route rather than greedily picking each disconnection.

name: R-SMILES
description: Root-aligned SMILES: a representation change that sharply improves seq2seq retrosynthesis accuracy by minimising the edit distance between product and reactants.

name: RetroSim
description: Similarity-based retrosynthesis: find precedent reactions for similar molecules and transfer the disconnection. The baseline every neural planner should beat, and often does not.

name: PaRoutes
description: Benchmark of real multi-step routes with the metrics to score a planner against them — how you tell whether a retrosynthesis model is actually better.

name: AiZynthTrain
description: Reproducible pipelines for training AiZynthFinder's models on your own reaction data, so in-house chemistry and stock are reflected in the routes.

name: Open Reaction Database
description: Open, structured reaction data with a defined schema — the public counterweight to proprietary reaction corpora, and the place to put your own.

name: DRFP
description: Reaction fingerprints without atom mapping or a neural net; a fast, surprisingly strong featuriser for yield and condition models.

name: SYBA
description: Bayesian classifier for synthetic accessibility trained on easy vs hard molecules — a different signal from SAscore, useful as a second opinion.

name: PostEra Manifold
description: Route search over purchasable space with prices and lead times, plus synthesis-aware analogue search. Free tier covers occasional use.

name: Spaya
description: Iktos' retrosynthesis service scoring routes on feasibility and building-block availability.

name: Synthia
description: Merck's expert-rules retrosynthesis platform (formerly Chematica) — hand-encoded chemistry rather than learned templates, and strong on stereochemistry.

name: Reaxys
description: Elsevier's reaction and substance database; the precedent search a chemist checks before trusting any predicted route.

name: eMolecules
description: Building-block and screening-compound catalogue with supplier stock and pricing, searchable by substructure.

name: Mcule
description: Purchasable compound database with per-compound availability and a free web tier for small searches.

name: Chemspace
description: Aggregated supplier space — in-stock screening compounds and make-on-demand building blocks in one search.

name: canSAR
description: Target assessment built for drug discovery rather than biology: structural druggability, existing chemistry, clinical precedent and safety signals for one protein on one page.

name: Probe Miner
description: Scores public chemical probes on potency, selectivity and cell activity, so you can tell whether the compound in a paper actually supports its conclusion.

name: FTMap
description: Computational solvent mapping: docks small organic probes across the surface to find consensus hot spots — where a ligand could get real binding energy, before any chemistry starts.

name: Fragment Hotspot Maps
description: CCDC's hotspot maps score a pocket by the interaction patterns seen in crystal structures, showing which subpockets are worth growing into.

name: DrugCentral
description: Approved drugs with their targets, measured activities, indications and pharmacology — the fastest way to see what already works on a target family.

name: Therapeutic Target Database
description: Targets classified by clinical stage with the drugs against each, useful for judging how contested a target already is.

name: PDBe-KB
description: Aggregates every structural annotation for a protein — ligand sites, interfaces, conformational states — across all its PDB entries at once.

name: KLIFS
description: Kinase-ligand structures on a common 85-residue binding-site numbering, so binding modes and DFG/αC states are comparable across the whole kinome.

name: GPCRdb
description: Structures, mutations, ligands and conformational states across the GPCR superfamily, on a shared residue numbering.

name: gnomAD
description: Population variation with loss-of-function constraint: whether humans tolerate losing this gene is the cheapest safety signal you will get on a target.

name: GWAS Catalog
description: Curated genotype-phenotype associations — the genetic evidence line that most strongly predicts clinical success.

name: STITCH
description: Known and predicted chemical-protein interactions across species, useful for a first pass at what else a chemotype might touch.

name: Chemprop
description: Directed message-passing neural networks for molecular property prediction — the open baseline that beats descriptor models on most endpoints with enough data, and the engine under ADMET-AI.

name: PanDDA
description: Finds fragment binding events that conventional refinement misses, by comparing many datasets to a ground state — the analysis that makes crystallographic fragment screening work at all.

name: Fragalysis
description: Diamond's browser for fragment screening campaigns: every hit, its density and its pose, in one place, with the merged designs that came from them.

name: SeeSAR
description: Interactive structure-based design: grow, replace and link with estimated affinity and torsion strain updating as you edit. The commercial tool medicinal chemists actually enjoy using.

name: HADDOCK3
description: Integrative docking driven by experimental restraints, and the practical open route to protein-protein and ternary complexes such as PROTAC-induced interfaces.

name: Cytoscape
description: The platform network pharmacology is done on: build a compound-target-pathway network, lay it out, score the hubs, and see what the topology actually says.

name: NetworkAnalyst
description: Network and enrichment analysis in the browser, from a gene or protein list to a protein-protein interaction subnetwork with statistics attached.

name: Metascape
description: Gene list annotation and enrichment across many ontologies at once, with a protein-protein interaction module. The fastest way from a hit list to a defensible pathway story.

name: GeneMANIA
description: Predicts function by placing a gene in a composite network of co-expression, physical interaction and pathway membership, and names the evidence for each edge.

name: clusterProfiler
description: The R package most enrichment figures in the literature come from: over-representation and GSEA across GO, KEGG and custom sets, with the plots built in.

name: CTD
description: Comparative Toxicogenomics Database: curated chemical-gene, chemical-disease and gene-disease relationships from the literature. The evidence layer under most chemical-centric network studies.

name: BATMAN-TCM
description: Predicts targets for the constituents of a herbal formula and runs the enrichment over them, built specifically for the multi-compound multi-target case.

name: NPASS
description: Natural products with measured activities against defined targets, and the species they came from. The quantitative counterpart to structure-only natural product collections.

name: CMAUP
description: Collective molecular activities of useful plants: plant species mapped to their constituents, those constituents to targets, and targets to pathways and diseases.

name: IMPPAT
description: Indian medicinal plants, their phytochemicals and therapeutic uses, with curated structures and drug-likeness already computed.

name: FooDB
description: The chemistry of food: constituents of plant and animal foods with structures, concentrations and provenance. Useful when the starting point is a dietary source rather than a screening deck.

name: Phenol-Explorer
description: Measured polyphenol contents of foods, including what processing and cooking do to them. Specific where general natural product databases are silent.

name: Open Babel
description: Chemical file format interconversion, 3D coordinate generation and conformer search across 110+ formats.

name: Datamol
description: Ergonomic RDKit wrapper for standardisation, featurisation and parallel molecular processing.

name: ChEMBL Structure Pipeline
description: The exact standardisation, parent-extraction and salt-stripping rules ChEMBL applies; the reference for reproducible curation.

name: Mordred
description: 1,800+ 2D/3D molecular descriptors on top of RDKit; the classical descriptor baseline for QSAR.

name: CDK
description: Chemistry Development Kit: the mature Java cheminformatics library (descriptors, fingerprints, IO).

name: Indigo
description: EPAM's cheminformatics toolkit for structure handling, reaction processing and rendering, with bindings for several languages.

name: Ketcher
description: Web structure editor for sketching molecules and reactions in browser-based apps.

name: OPSIN
description: Converts IUPAC chemical names to structures; the standard name-to-structure parser.

name: DataWarrior
description: Free desktop app for chemical data visualisation, SAR analysis, clustering and property prediction.

name: CReM
description: Chemically reasonable mutations: fragment-based structure generation with medicinal-chemistry-valid replacements.

name: molSimplify
description: Builds, optimises and screens transition-metal complexes from a metal, oxidation state and ligand set; generates sane 3D geometries where general-purpose toolkits guess badly.

name: Architector
description: Generates 3D conformers for metal complexes across the periodic table, including multiple spin states and coordination geometries, as a Python API.

name: Cambridge Structural Database (CCDC)
description: The small-molecule crystal structure archive, over half of it metal-organic. The empirical reference for coordination geometry, bond lengths and ligand conformation.

name: ChEMBL
description: Manually curated bioactivity database (~2.4M compounds, 20M+ activities) mapped to targets and assays.

name: PubChem
description: The largest open chemical database: compounds, substances, bioassays, patents and literature links.

name: ZINC22
description: Purchasable and make-on-demand compounds prepared for docking in 3D, at tens of billions of molecules.

name: Enamine REAL Space
description: Make-on-demand combinatorial space of 6B+ synthesisable compounds with ~80% synthesis success.

name: DrugBank
description: Approved and investigational drugs with targets, pharmacology, interactions and ADMET; free academic tier.

name: BindingDB
description: Measured binding affinities (Kd/Ki/IC50) for protein-small molecule pairs, curated from literature and patents.

name: PDBbind+
description: Experimental binding affinities paired with their PDB complex structures; the basis of the CASF scoring benchmarks (the old pdbbind.org.cn is retired).

name: Papyrus
description: A normalised, standardised bioactivity dataset (60M+ points) assembled for ML-ready QSAR modelling — the cleaned-up ChEMBL you were going to build yourself.

name: SureChEMBL
description: Chemical structures extracted from patents, updated daily; the standard patent-chemistry search.

name: COCONUT
description: Aggregated open natural products collection with structures and source organisms.

name: GtoPdb (Guide to Pharmacology)
description: Expert-curated ligand-target pharmacology: selectivity, affinities and recommended tool compounds.

name: Chemical Probes Portal
description: Expert review of which chemical probes are actually fit for target validation, and at what concentration.

name: smina
description: Vina fork with flexible scoring-function specification and much easier custom-term development.

name: Vina-GPU 2.1
description: GPU-parallel Vina, and the QuickVina2-GPU variant alongside it, giving one to two orders of magnitude speedup on large screens.

name: Uni-Dock
description: GPU-accelerated docking engine reaching thousands of molecules per second per GPU.

name: DOCK 6
description: UCSF's long-standing anchor-and-grow docking program with a wide scoring-function suite.

name: rDock
description: Fast open-source docking for proteins and nucleic acids, with pharmacophore and tethered-scaffold restraints.

name: Meeko
description: Prepares ligands and receptors for AutoDock: PDBQT writing, macrocycle handling, covalent setups.

name: Ringtail
description: Stores and filters millions of docking results in SQLite so large screens stay queryable.

name: VirtualFlow
description: Open workflow for distributing ultra-large virtual screens (billions of ligands) across HPC and cloud.

name: EasyDock
description: Python wrapper unifying Vina/smina/gnina runs with SQLite bookkeeping and protonation handling.

name: DockStream
description: AstraZeneca's docking wrapper exposing several backends to generative loops such as REINVENT.

name: ODDT
description: Open Drug Discovery Toolkit: rescoring functions (RFScore, NNScore), interaction fingerprints and VS metrics.

name: PLIP
description: Detects and reports non-covalent protein-ligand interactions from a complex; standard for pose interpretation.

name: LigPlot+
description: 2D schematic diagrams of protein-ligand interactions for figures and pose triage.

name: Glide (Schrödinger)
description: Industry-standard commercial docking (HTVS/SP/XP) with the Maestro preparation stack.

name: GOLD (CCDC)
description: Genetic-algorithm docking with CSD-derived knowledge and well-validated scoring functions.

name: MOE (CCG)
description: Integrated commercial modelling environment: docking, pharmacophores, biologics and QSAR in one platform.

name: SwissDock
description: Free docking web service (AutoDock Vina and Attracting Cavities backends) for occasional runs.

name: Pharmit
description: Interactive pharmacophore and shape search over billions of purchasable compounds, with in-browser minimisation.

name: MetalDock
description: Docks organometallic and metal-complex ligands into proteins, DNA and other biomolecules, optimising the complex with QM and generating the metal parameters the docking needs.

name: AutoDock4Zn
description: Zinc force field for AutoDock4 adding directional pseudo-atoms around the ion, so tetrahedral coordination is rewarded geometrically rather than as undirected electrostatics.

name: gnina
description: Fork of smina with convolutional neural network scoring and rescoring, run alongside the empirical score rather than instead of it.

name: GaudiMM
description: Multi-objective genetic algorithm that optimises binding, geometry and any other objective you define at once, instead of collapsing them into one score. Handles metal coordination and flexible systems that fixed-receptor docking cannot express.

name: GROMACS
description: The most widely used open MD engine; fast on CPU and GPU, with a complete analysis toolchain.

name: AMBER / AmberTools
description: Amber force fields and simulation stack; AmberTools is free, pmemd.CUDA is licensed.

name: NAMD
description: Scalable MD for very large systems on HPC, paired with VMD for setup and analysis.

name: CHARMM-GUI
description: Web system builder that sets up membranes, glycans, ligands and solvated systems for every major MD engine.

name: MDAnalysis
description: Python library for reading and analysing trajectories from essentially every MD format.

name: MDTraj
description: Fast trajectory IO and geometric analysis with a lightweight NumPy-native API.

name: PLUMED
description: Plugin for enhanced sampling and free-energy methods (metadynamics, umbrella sampling) across MD engines.

name: OpenFF Toolkit
description: Open Force Field small-molecule parameterisation with direct OpenMM/GROMACS export.

name: ACPYPE
description: Converts Antechamber/GAFF ligand parameters into GROMACS, CHARMM and other topologies.

name: ParmEd
description: Reads, edits and converts parameter/topology files between AMBER, CHARMM, GROMACS and OpenMM.

name: gmx_MMPBSA
description: MM-PBSA/MM-GBSA end-state binding free energies from GROMACS trajectories, with per-residue decomposition.

name: OpenFE
description: Open Free Energy: production relative and absolute binding free-energy campaigns with reproducible protocols.

name: BioSimSpace
description: Interoperable layer for building and running MD and alchemical free-energy workflows across engines.

name: alchemlyb
description: Standard estimators (MBAR, BAR, TI) and convergence diagnostics for alchemical free-energy data.

name: FEP+ (Schrödinger)
description: Commercial relative binding free-energy platform, the industry reference for lead-optimisation potency prediction.

name: MACE / MACE-OFF
description: Equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials, including transferable organic force fields for biomolecular systems.

name: TorchANI
description: PyTorch implementation of the ANI neural network potentials for organic molecules.

name: Espaloma
description: Graph-neural-network force-field parameter assignment, replacing atom typing with learned chemistry.

name: OpenMM-ML
description: Mixed ML/MM simulation in OpenMM: treat the ligand with a neural potential and the rest classically.

name: Martini
description: Coarse-grained force field for large-scale membrane, protein and lipid-nanoparticle simulation.

name: GaMD
description: Gaussian accelerated MD: adds a harmonic boost potential to flatten energy barriers, reaching microsecond-scale conformational transitions without a predefined reaction coordinate. Implemented in AMBER, NAMD and OpenMM.

name: gamd-openmm
description: The OpenMM implementation of GaMD — the easiest route to accelerated sampling on a GPU without leaving Python.

name: WESTPA
description: Weighted ensemble sampling: runs many short trajectories with statistical reweighting to reach rare events and extract rate constants, rather than waiting for one long trajectory to cross the barrier.

name: SuMD
description: Supervised MD: biases nothing but discards trajectories heading the wrong way, so ligand binding and unbinding pathways emerge in accessible wall-clock time.

name: OpenPathSampling
description: Transition path sampling and interface sampling for rare events where you care about the mechanism and rate, not just the endpoints.

name: openmmtools
description: Replica exchange, alchemical factories and well-tested integrators for OpenMM — the standard way to run REST2/parallel tempering in Python.

name: mdpocket
description: The fpocket companion that tracks pocket volume and persistence across an MD trajectory — how you find a cryptic pocket that only opens some of the time.

name: PocketMiner
description: Predicts where cryptic pockets are likely to open from a single structure, so you know whether long sampling is worth running at all.

name: deeptime
description: Markov state models, TICA/VAMP and kinetic analysis of long or many-replica trajectories.

name: MCPB.py
description: AmberTools' metal centre parameter builder: derives bonded-model force field parameters for a metal site from QM, the standard route to simulating a metalloprotein without the ion drifting out.

name: easyPARM
description: Automates force field parameter derivation for metal complexes and organometallics from a QM optimisation, producing ready-to-run Amber, GROMACS, CHARMM and OpenMM inputs.

name: GPathFinder
description: Finds the route a ligand takes in and out of a buried site by multi-objective search over GaudiMM, giving binding pathways and intermediate poses rather than only the bound state.

name: OMMProtocol
description: Runs a complete OpenMM pipeline, from minimisation through equilibration to production, from one YAML file, with checkpointing and standard reporters.

name: Psi4
description: Open-source quantum chemistry (DFT, MP2, CC) with a Python API suited to automated workflows.

name: PySCF
description: Python-native electronic structure library, easy to embed in ML and screening pipelines.

name: ORCA
description: Broad-capability QM package, free for academic use; common for spectroscopy and mechanism work.

name: xtb
description: Semiempirical GFNn-xTB methods: geometry, frequencies and energies fast enough for thousands of molecules.

name: CREST
description: Conformer-rotamer ensemble sampling on top of xtb; the standard cheap conformational search.

name: NWChem
description: Scalable HPC quantum chemistry for large systems and plane-wave/molecular hybrids.

name: autodE
description: Automated reaction-profile generation: conformers, transition states and barriers with minimal manual setup.

name: Garleek
description: Bridges Gaussian's ONIOM to molecular mechanics backends such as Tinker and OpenMM, so a QM/MM job can put a metal centre in the QM layer and the rest of the protein in MM.

name: ESIgen
description: Turns raw quantum chemistry output into a formatted supporting information document: geometries, energies, frequencies and images, from a template.

name: pysisyphus
description: Optimises stationary points on reaction paths: chain-of-states methods, transition state searches and intrinsic reaction coordinates, driving whichever QM engine you have.

name: Multiwfn
description: Wavefunction analysis: bond orders, charges, orbital composition, electron density topology and non-covalent interaction plots from the output of most QM programs.

name: MOSES
description: Benchmarking platform for molecular generative models with standard splits and distribution metrics.

name: GuacaMol
description: Goal-directed and distribution-learning benchmarks for de novo design, still the common comparison point.

name: SAFE
description: Sequential attachment-based fragment embedding: a SMILES rewrite that makes scaffold-constrained generation natural.

name: Pocket2Mol
description: Equivariant generation of 3D molecules conditioned directly on a binding pocket.

name: DiffLinker
description: Equivariant diffusion for linker design in fragment linking and PROTAC-style problems.

name: LigandMPNN
description: Sequence design conditioned on ligands, nucleotides and cofactors; the successor to ProteinMPNN for binding sites.

name: DEL-iver
description: Processes DNA-encoded library selections: building-block and disynthon enrichment, binding models on building-block or full-molecule inputs, and analog picking from make-on-demand space. Early research code from a 2026 preprint. The default split is random, which leaks building blocks between train and test, so re-split by building block before trusting the AUROC.

name: scikit-mol
description: RDKit featurisation wrapped as scikit-learn transformers, so fingerprints and descriptors live inside a Pipeline and cannot leak across a split.

name: DeepChem
description: Long-running deep learning library for chemistry and biology: featurisers, splitters, model zoo and the MoleculeNet task collection.

name: QSARtuna
description: AstraZeneca's automated QSAR model building: preprocessing, algorithm and hyperparameter search, uncertainty.

name: Uni-Mol
description: 3D-aware molecular representation model used as a pretrained backbone for property and binding tasks.

name: MolSkill
description: Learns medicinal chemists' implicit preferences from pairwise choices to score compound attractiveness.

name: PyTorch Geometric
description: The standard GNN library for molecular graphs: message passing, pooling, batching over molecules.

name: DGL-LifeSci
description: Ready-made GNN models and datasets for property prediction, reaction prediction and generation.

name: Optuna
description: Hyperparameter optimisation with pruning; the usual companion to model selection in QSAR pipelines.

name: scikit-learn
description: The classical ML baseline stack (RF, SVM, calibration, CV) that every QSAR study is measured against.

name: XGBoost
description: Gradient boosting that remains highly competitive on descriptor/fingerprint tabular chemistry data.

name: KNIME
description: Visual workflow platform with mature chemistry nodes (RDKit, Schrödinger, Vernalis) for no-code pipelines.

name: CheMeleon
description: Foundation model pretrained to reproduce Mordred descriptors, then fine-tuned through Chemprop with --from-foundation CheMeleon; beats descriptor and GNN baselines on small property datasets.

name: Mol-JEPA
description: Boehringer Ingelheim's multimodal joint-embedding model, fusing cellular effects, binding affinity, ADMET and quantum chemistry into one molecular representation. Code is unlicensed; the weights are CC BY-NC 4.0.

name: ADMETlab 3.0
description: Web predictor covering 88 ADMET endpoints with uncertainty estimates and batch submission.

name: SwissADME
description: Fast physicochemical, pharmacokinetic and drug-likeness profiling including the BOILED-Egg permeability model.

name: pkCSM
description: Graph-signature-based ADMET prediction across absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicity endpoints.

name: ProTox 3.0
description: Toxicity endpoint prediction (organ toxicity, endpoints, pathways, LD50) with similarity and fragment evidence.

name: vNN-ADMET
description: Variable-nearest-neighbour ADMET models with explicit applicability domain, including DILI and CYP endpoints.

name: OPERA
description: Free, regulatory-grade QSAR models for physchem and ADMET endpoints with applicability domain and AD-based confidence; used by EPA/NIH.

name: Open Systems Pharmacology (PK-Sim/MoBi)
description: Open-source PBPK and QSP modelling suite; the free alternative to commercial PBPK platforms.

name: Simcyp (Certara)
description: Commercial PBPK simulator used in regulatory submissions for DDI and special-population predictions.

name: GastroPlus
description: Commercial PBPK/absorption simulation, standard for formulation and oral bioavailability modelling.

name: ASKCOS
description: MIT's open retrosynthesis, forward prediction and condition recommendation platform.

name: Syntheseus
description: Benchmarking and inference framework that puts retrosynthesis models on a common, fairly evaluated footing.

name: IBM RXN for Chemistry
description: Transformer-based forward prediction, retrosynthesis and procedure generation as a free web service.

name: rdchiral
description: Correct chirality handling when applying retrosynthetic reaction templates in RDKit.

name: SCScore
description: Synthetic complexity score learned from reaction corpora, complementing the classic SA score.

name: RAscore
description: Predicts whether a retrosynthesis planner would find a route, as a fast synthesisability filter.

name: PyRosetta
description: Python interface to Rosetta for design, docking, loop modelling and energy calculations; free academic licence.

name: RosettaCommons
description: The Rosetta software suite for macromolecular modelling and design, and its licensing/community hub.

name: Protein-Sol
description: Sequence-based prediction of heterologous expression solubility in E. coli, scaled against an experimental set; a cheap first read on whether a construct will express before anyone orders it.

name: ANARCI
description: Antibody numbering and germline assignment (IMGT, Kabat, Chothia); the preprocessing step for antibody ML.

name: ImmuneBuilder
description: Fast antibody, nanobody and TCR structure prediction with accuracy competitive on CDR loops.

name: AbLang2
description: Antibody language model for restoring missing residues and generating germline-plausible sequences.

name: SAbDab / SAbPred
description: Curated structural antibody database plus the OPIG prediction suite (paratope, epitope, developability, TAP).

name: Observed Antibody Space (OAS)
description: Billions of cleaned, numbered antibody repertoire sequences; the pretraining corpus for antibody models.

name: IgBLAST
description: NCBI's immunoglobulin/TCR V(D)J assignment tool for repertoire sequencing.

name: FoldX
description: Empirical force field for fast stability and binding ddG on point mutations; free academic licence.

name: ESM
description: Evolutionary-scale protein language models, used for embeddings, variant effect scores and as the front end of structure prediction without an MSA.

name: FireProt
description: Automated design of thermostable variants, combining energy- and evolution-based predictions into a short list of mutations worth making rather than a ranked dump of all of them.

name: ThermoMPNN
description: Graph network predicting the change in folding stability for every point mutation in a structure, fast enough to scan a whole protein.

name: Therapeutics Data Commons
description: 66+ AI-ready therapeutic datasets with fixed splits and leaderboards, spanning ADMET to biologics.

name: MoleculeNet
description: The original standard property-prediction benchmark suite (ESOL, FreeSolv, BACE, Tox21, …).

name: DUD-E
description: Directory of useful decoys, enhanced: actives with property-matched decoys for virtual-screening evaluation.

name: LIT-PCBA
description: Unbiased virtual screening benchmark built from dose-response PubChem assays, designed to avoid DUD-E's biases.

name: PoseCheck
description: Physical-plausibility checks (strain energy, steric clashes, interactions) for structure-based generative models.

name: Polaris
description: Community platform for rigorous, versioned benchmarks in drug-discovery ML with leak-resistant splits.

name: ClinicalTrials.gov
description: Registry of 500k+ trials with a modern API; the source for competitive and trial-design landscaping.

name: openFDA
description: APIs over FDA drug labels, adverse events (FAERS), recalls and device data.

name: Drugs@FDA
description: Approval history, review documents and labels for FDA-approved drugs.

name: EMA Medicines
description: European public assessment reports and product information for centrally authorised medicines.

name: DailyMed
description: Current FDA structured product labels (SPL), machine-readable and updated daily.

name: SIDER
description: Side-effect resource linking marketed drugs to label-extracted adverse reactions and frequencies.

name: Europe PMC
description: Full-text life-science literature with annotations and a solid API for text mining.

name: PubMed / NCBI E-utilities
description: Biomedical citation index and the E-utilities API behind most literature pipelines.

name: Google Patents
description: Full-text patent search across the major offices with chemical structure indexing; the practical first look at whether a scaffold is already claimed.

name: Espacenet
description: The European Patent Office's search over 140 million patent documents, with family and legal-status data that the free aggregators do not carry.

name: Nextflow
description: Dataflow workflow engine with containerised, resumable execution across HPC and cloud; nf-core supplies vetted pipelines.

name: Snakemake
description: Python-based workflow manager with conda/container integration, common for bioinformatics pipelines.

name: MLflow
description: Experiment tracking, model registry and packaging; the usual answer to 'which model made this prediction'.

name: DVC
description: Git-style versioning for datasets and model artefacts, so screening data stays reproducible.

name: Ray
description: Distributed execution for parallel docking, simulation sweeps and model training on one API.

name: Dask
description: Parallel dataframes and task graphs for larger-than-memory chemical datasets.

name: PyTorch Lightning
description: Training-loop framework that standardises multi-GPU training and checkpointing for molecular models.

name: Hugging Face Hub
description: Where most released protein and molecule model weights and datasets now live.

name: PyChimera
description: Use the UCSF Chimera Python API from an ordinary interpreter, so Chimera's structure handling can be scripted inside a normal pipeline instead of its own shell.

name: Tangram
description: A suite of UCSF Chimera extensions from the same group: QM and QM/MM setup, PLIP interaction depiction, PropKa states, normal modes, and dummy-atom preparation of metal systems for MD. Free for academic use.

name: PyMOL (open source)
description: The de facto structure viewer for figures and pose inspection; open-source build plus a commercial edition.

name: UCSF ChimeraX
description: Modern successor to Chimera: large structures, cryo-EM maps, AlphaFold integration and scripting.

name: VMD
description: Trajectory visualisation and analysis for MD, with scripting and rendering for publication figures.

name: Mol*
description: The web molecular viewer used by RCSB and PDBe; embeddable in any internal tool.

name: NGL Viewer
description: Lightweight WebGL structure viewer, and the nglview Jupyter widget built on it.

name: 3Dmol.js
description: WebGL structure viewer, and through its py3Dmol binding the quickest way to eyeball docking poses inside a notebook.
